title: CI fails a change when a secret has aged past its rotation-days budget
description: A rotation gate runs in CI on every change. For each manifest entry with a `rotationDays` value, the gate compares the vendor-reported last-rotated timestamp against the current CI-run wall clock; a gap greater than `rotationDays` fails the run with a stable-coded error naming the logical name, the environment, the last-rotated timestamp, and the elapsed days. The gate has a documented override for a scheduled rotation window (an operator-authored justification file the gate reads with an expiry timestamp), and the override is itself audited. The gate runs on the manifest as-committed against the vendor as-configured; a required secret with no vendor-reported last-rotated timestamp fails the gate.
rationale: Rotation policies that are not enforced are policies that quietly slip. CI is the gate every change already passes through, and failing on staleness turns 'we should rotate this' into 'this change cannot merge until we do'. The override with an expiry keeps a legitimate mid-rotation change unblocked without opening a permanent bypass.
